import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 202

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/202](https://www.erdosproblems.com/202)
- [BFV13] de la Bretèche, Régis and Ford, Kevin and Vandehey, Joseph, *On non-intersecting
  arithmetic progressions*. Acta Arith. (2013), 381-392.
- [Ch05] Chen, Yong-Gao, *On disjoint arithmetic progressions*. Acta Arith. (2005), 143-148.
- [Cr03b] Croot, III, Ernest S., *On non-intersecting arithmetic progressions*. Acta Arith.
  (2003), 233-238.
- [ErSz68] Erdős, P. and Szemerédi, E., *On a problem of P. Erdős and S. Stein*. Acta Arith.
  (1968), 85-90.
- [PaPh24] Park, Jinyoung and Pham, Huy Tuan, *A proof of the Kahn-Kalai conjecture*. J. Amer.
  Math. Soc. (2024), 235-243.
-/

open Filter Real

namespace Erdos202

/--
`f N` is the maximum possible `r` such that there are moduli $n_1<\cdots<n_r\leq N$ with
associated residues $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ whose congruence classes are disjoint.
-/
noncomputable def f (N : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {r : ℕ | ∃ n : Fin r → ℕ, ∃ a : Fin r → ℤ,
    StrictMono n ∧ (∀ i, 0 < n i ∧ n i ≤ N) ∧
    ∀ m : ℤ, ∀ i j : Fin r, m ≡ a i [ZMOD (n i : ℤ)] → m ≡ a j [ZMOD (n j : ℤ)] → i = j}

/--
Let $n_1<\cdots < n_r\leq N$ with associated $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ such that the congruence classes are
disjoint (that is, every integer is $\equiv a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for at most one $1\leq i\leq r$). How
large can $r$ be in terms of $N$?

Let $f(N)$ be the maximum possible $r$, and let $L(N)=\exp(\sqrt{\log N\log\log N})$.

This was proved by GPT-5.4 Pro (prompted by Ho Boon Suan), using the argument of [BFV13] together
with the resolution of the Kahn-Kalai conjecture by Park and Pham [PaPh24], so that
$$f(N)= N L(N)^{-1+o(1)}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos202.lean"]
theorem erdos_202 : ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, (f N : ℝ) = (N : ℝ) * scaleL N ^ (-1 + o N) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Stein conjectured that $f(N)=o(N)$, which was proved by Erdős and Szemerédi [ErSz68].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_202.variants.erdos_szemeredi :
    (fun N => (f N : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun N : ℕ => (N : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos202

reformulations.difference: The informal exponent −1+o(1) is represented by a single real-valued error sequence, little-o of the constant function 1, together with eventual exact equality.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For sufficiently large N, N>0 and L(N)>1. The Lean statement is equivalent to: for every ε>0, eventually N·L(N)^(−1−ε) ≤ f(N) ≤ N·L(N)^(−1+ε). Forward, use |o(N)|≤ε and monotonicity in the exponent. Conversely, the lower bound ensures eventual positivity, and o(N)=1+log_{L(N)}(f(N)/N) gives the equality; the two bounds force |o(N)|≤ε eventually. This equivalence was proved independently as Review202.main_asymptotic_iff_bounds in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using either problem theorem.

review.notes:
All three declarations match the cited mathematics. Independent Lean checks establish that the admissible cardinalities form a nonempty set bounded by N, so f is an attained maximum rather than a default-valued supremum. They also establish f(0)=0, f(1)=f(2)=1, a two-class example at N=4, the disjointness characterization, and the historical variant's equivalence to f(N)/N → 0. All scratch proofs compile without sorryAx. An exhaustive finite search agrees with OEIS for 1≤N≤16.

Both solved tags agree with the current source, which explicitly records SOLVED (LEAN). The linked proof uses an equivalent finite-set maximum and epsilon-bound formulation and contains no explicit admissions or custom axiom declarations. Independent kernel revalidation of that external artifact was not completed: it targets Lean/Mathlib 4.29.1, while the sandbox uses 4.33.1 and reports compatibility/elaboration errors. This limitation does not establish a mathematical or status defect. Detailed checks are in /workspace/review/review-notes.md; the reviewed file is unchanged.
